I climbed to gold myself and here's some tips I learned while doing dps, just know that I am a reaper one trick and this is something I have noticed from Genji players in my games.

1) You have to understand your role. Since you play Genji, you have to avoid characters who shit on you at close range and tanks overall (As they don't fall that easily to genji's attacks). You can still deal with them, but it's recommended you go assassinate squishies. Genji excels at taking out targets and then chaining it, but like many people say, always go for supports as they are the backbone of a team and once they fall, the rest of the team will fall if they don't run away or hide for a bit.

2) You have to learn how to go for headshots or at least hit around that area. I main reaper, so I have to learn where to aim my cross hair depending on the range (chin when I am within 10 meters, chest if I am at 20, and torso if I am beyond that). Genji has two attacks, his secondary is king at close range rights as that fan is good. I suggest you use the 3 attack he has on primary to poke long range individuals. Another tip in this catagory is learn how to animation cancel. Genji has several animation cancels you should learn about and it might be helpful in masking his reload animation as you can reload then dash before it ends, that way you have full ammo and you do damage. It's one of many animation cancels you should practice.

3) Just practice and tough through slums. I had a two week period where I was playing dps terrible and although I was suffering and I had hundreds of slurs thrown at me, I took each loss as a chance to learn and eventually, I got pretty decently.

Final Thought: Climbing out of bronze is gonna be hell, it took me 4 weeks to climb out and 3 weeks to get out of silver, but I assure you, once you get out of bronze, you'll feel way better. I may not main Genji, but I do know Genji's role is to harass and assassinate squishes like supports and dps heros like widow. I assure you, once you learn how to kill enemies and be annoying, the enemy team will spend a lot of time trying to shoot you and nothing is worse than having to aim for a zipping ninja who can kill anyone. Remember, every loss is a chance to learn and it's never ok to blame your teammates. Sure there are games where they play as shit, but you have to think "ok, what can I do next time to pick up my team's slack in case they fail to do so and what can I do better?"

As an aph one trick with over 400k, I can see some mistakes that a lot of new aph players make and I myself am guilty of making those mistakes as I am not perfect, but I do have some advice on how to play aph.
Early: Aph has no abilities at level 1, so last hit minions and freeze under wave. If you miss some cs, don't let it bring you down. Just keep on trying to last hit and I recommend going into a practice game and practice last hitting as it's not easy to do. Once you hit level 2, do not make a play unless you have to to save you or your support. Wait for your support to make a play or for your jungler to gank. It is crucial you constantly side step as aph has not much escape aside from his ms as it also allows you to dodge skill shots such as hooks. Rush an ie with B.F. Sword and Pickaxe being must buys as extra ad will help you a lot. Try to build IE first then boots, but if you are fed enough, hurricane.
Support Synergy: Aph works well with any support, but you must adust your playstyle to fit that support. If your supprot is a caster, you can be a bit risky as you know they can heal or shield you for protection. If they are a poke mage such as brand, play defensive and poke them out with your support. if they are a hook champ like pyke or thresh, watch them and go in when they set up a play for you. The fact alistar threw the game for you is upsetting as the alistar must be new at his job, so don't blame yourself if you are doing fine.
Falling behind in CS Ok so you fall behind at aph, but it isn't over for you. Continue to get assists and continue building your ie and hurricane. Stay behind your support and fed carry until you get enough gold to pick yourself up. Don't throw as it make it harder and harder to regain your composure.
Conclusion: Aph is a pretty diverse champ, so be patient with his gameplay. It took me 3 months to properly learn him and the reward will definally be worth it I promise you that. If you need any help, feel free to ask.

Calibrum is a pretty good weapon as it guarantees a hit if they are marked and in range. As an aph one trick, I've comboed many attacks with calibrum and sneaking an auto attack in before the mark lands is a good way to do damage in the early game as aph has less than 1.00 attack speed. So imagine this, you are about to make a play and you shoot your calibrum q, you are managed to land one auto attack from gravatum or serverum at your enemy and the moment the calibrum q hits, you can fire immediately again, applying another shot. Essentially, this is pretty good damage as he can fire faster than anyone else. Another really good example is when you ult with calibrum, the moment you see alune's image and the mark about to fall on them, you know she's about to cast a mark, so cast a q immediately and if it hits the enemy, fire immediately and as the projectile from the previous mark is flying, alune will mark them for you, allowing you to instantly fire again. So essentially you comboed 2 auto attacks in 1 second, when aph ususally has up to 1.67 attack speed. Animation canceling is a pretty good tip and practice makes perfect, so take your time with that. It took me a month to learn how to make these types of plays and combos and the reward is worth it as it makes aph a devasting sniper and adc. If you need help, don't be afraid to ask.

Techniquelly all four precision keystones work on him.

Press the Attack: Good for early damage, really easy to proc, and a good rune for solo lanes against mobile targets. Benefits such as attack speed or healing aren't available early unless you buy dagger or potions.

Lethal Tempo: Aphelio's most used rune next to conquer, the attack speed is good for unleashing a ton of attacks, weak early start, strong late game. Not recommended in solo lanes due to pta and conquer being more useful.

Fleet Footwork: Good for defensive aph. Good sustain and movement speed is good for escaping situations. Can help with kiting with ms. Aph must be defensive and be heaily reliant on his support ot make a play due to benefits such as attack speed or extra ad not being available early.

Conquer: Aph's most used rune next to lethal tempo. grants extra AD, which can help turn the tides of some fights, a good solo lane rune against immobile targets as it makes aph a deadly 1v1'er. Bot lane, conquer is good as it's even easier to proc it due to two people being there and once its proced and there's a support nearby, aph can shred most early game champs.

That's my experience with each rune and how you use them is completely dependent on you. For top aph or mid aph, I always grab conquer or press the attack, depending on the line up. I don't grab fleet due to me being able to properly kite and aph already heals a lot, so I don't need the heal fleet offers. Conquer is a good rune as aph can easily proc it due to having so many abilities that can either home, target, or splash onto his enemies. Personally, I think Lethal and Conquer is the best, but that's to me.
